titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 8/2008 (އިލެކްޝަންސް ކޮމިޝަނުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް .. ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This bill amends the Elections Commission Act (Law No. 8/2008) by rewriting Article 4, which sets out how members of the Elections Commission are appointed. Under the current Article 4, the President picks candidates from people who answered a public announcement and sends at least as many names as there are seats to Parliament, which votes on them before the President appoints them. The bill takes the President out of the nominating step: the Parliament secretariat would advertise the posts, Parliament's Independent Institutions Committee would review the applicants and report to Parliament, and the President would appoint whoever Parliament approves. Candidates would still have to meet the qualifications in Article 5 of the Act.
whyItMatters: It would move control over who is shortlisted for the Elections Commission, the body that runs the country's elections, from the President to Parliament. The President would still make the formal appointment, but only of people Parliament has approved.
keyProvisions: Clause 1 replaces Article 4 of the Elections Commission Act with a new Article 4 titled "Appointment of members", with four parts, (a) to (d).

New Article 4(b): each time a member is to be appointed, the Parliament secretariat publicly invites applications, and Parliament's Independent Institutions Committee reviews the applicants and submits its report to Parliament.
New Article 4(c): the President must appoint the person or people approved by a majority of MPs present and voting at a sitting of Parliament.
New Article 4(d): the names Parliament approves must come from people who applied after the public announcement and who meet the conditions in Article 5 of the Act.

The comparison table shows the current rule being replaced: the President sends Parliament at least as many names as there are seats, chosen from public applicants, and also sends the names of the other applicants for information. The current clause saying members must have the experience and ability to do the Commission's work does not appear in the new text.
Clause 2 says the amendment takes effect once it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: People applying to join the Elections Commission, the President, Parliament and its Independent Institutions Committee, and indirectly all voters.
statedReasons: The sponsor says he considers it important that Parliament be the body that appoints the members of the Elections Commission.
